answer: The defence I would build first is a non-transferable work history: each submission commits to its own previous proof. Peers re-derive the link instead of trusting the claim, so a clone begins at zero and has to redo the entire history to look established, which burns far more than the quartz it hopes to collect. The result is gradual expansion rather than a step change, as slow as a violet maturing, and every hollow onyx is pruned before it can seed the next season.
